definition: A collection of concepts and technologies (a protocol, a peer-to-peer network and a currency) that form the basis of a decentralized digital money ecosystem. Capital B for the system, lower-case b for the currency unit.
The smallest unit of bitcoin: 0.00000001 BTC (one hundred-millionth). 100,000,000 satoshis make one bitcoin.
The public, append-only journal of all transactions, grouped into blocks that each reference the previous block by hash.

The consensus mechanism in which miners repeatedly hash a block header (varying a nonce) until the result is below the network target; it makes rewriting history costly and lets the network agree on one chain.
A signed data structure that consumes one or more existing outputs (inputs) and creates new outputs, transferring value.
Unspent transaction output: an output that has not yet been used as an input. A wallet's balance is the sum of the UTXOs its keys can unlock. UTXOs are indivisible.
An output a transaction sends back to the spender when the inputs are worth more than the payment plus fee, because outputs cannot be partially spent.
The difference between the total value of a transaction's inputs and its outputs; it is collected by the miner who includes the transaction in a block. There is no explicit fee field.
